prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: single production 2D Spine forehead-fringe attachment
Input image: Image 1 defines the original character's silver-white short bob, asymmetrical fringe and restrained flat Live2D color treatment. Use only those identity and palette cues.
Primary request: Draw exactly one connected, bangs-only hair strip for a three-quarter-view fantasy mage facing screen-right. The physical silhouette is a low horizontal arch about 2.5 times wider than tall. It contains one broad tapered center bang sweeping diagonally toward screen-left, four smaller forehead points, one short temple point at each end, and a plain connected overlap flap along the upper edge. The overlap flap is 12 percent of the piece height and will be hidden under another hair layer. Empty gaps between the lower tips must remain unpainted so separate eyes and glasses can show through.
Rendering: production game texture source, unlit matte cel paint, three flat color groups only: silver-white base, pale-lavender shadow, and thin cool-gray physical contour. Use hard fill boundaries and at most one normal antialiasing pixel along the physical edge. All rendered pixels must belong to the hair itself. There is no lighting effect around the piece and no soft transition beyond its contour.
Composition/framing: exactly one shallow fringe strip, centered, uncropped, with broad unused margin on all four sides. The result must not resemble a complete head covering.
Constraints: no complete hairstyle, wig, crown dome, rear hair, nape hair, bob shell, long side hair, face, forehead skin, eyes, glasses, eyebrows, ears, neck, torso, clothing, hand, butterfly, ribbon, bow, hairpin, second piece, duplicate view, aura, outer glow, bloom, rim light, backlight, luminous outline, diffuse fringe, feathering, haze, fog, smoke, particles, cast shadow, drop shadow, floor, scenery, text, letters, numbers, logo, signature or watermark. No sprite sheet, atlas page, turnaround, panel grid, inset image or multiple views.
